title: Apollo's charts still show no AI payoff outside the tech giants
friendlyTitle: Apollo's charts still show no AI payoff outside the biggest tech firms
summary: Torsten Slok, Apollo's chief economist, published a 24 October note arguing that AI spending has not yet shown up in the rest of corporate America. In the charts he posts, revenue per worker and profit margins are rising for the Magnificent Seven and flat for the other 493 companies in the S&P 500. He also shows a productivity series with no visible AI bump. His reading is that mainstream firms are starting to treat token spend as a cost, not a growth engine, and that the AI story will be decided outside the tech sector.
friendlySummary: Torsten Slok, Apollo's chief economist, published a note on 24 October. He argues that AI spending has not yet shown up in the rest of corporate America. In the charts he posts, revenue per worker and profit margins are rising for the seven biggest tech firms and flat for the other 493 companies in the S&P 500. He also shows a productivity series with no visible AI bump. His reading is that ordinary firms are starting to treat token spend as a cost, not a growth engine. He says the AI story will be decided outside the tech sector.
whyItMatters: If your company is being told to buy the newest model because the economy has already been transformed, these charts are a reason to ask for the line that moved. They are one economist's reading of public market data, not a controlled study of adoption. A flat margin is not proof that a specific workflow cannot pay. It is evidence that, so far, the payoff is still concentrated in the firms selling the tools.
